Driving Innovation</h3><ul style=\"min-height:1.5em\"><li><p style=\"min-height:1.5em\">Drive customer adoption of Float’s full suite of features, ensuring teams maximize the value of corporate and employee spend management.</p></li><li><p style=\"min-height:1.5em\">Advocate for customer participation in Float’s Early Adopter Programs, gathering insights to shape future product iterations.</p></li><li><p style=\"min-height:1.5em\">Educate and inspire customers to explore new ways to optimize their workflows with Float’s evolving capabilities.</p></li><li><p style=\"min-height:1.5em\">Identify opportunities for growth across your aligned Book of Business. </p></li></ul><h3>Being the Voice of the Customer at Float</h3><ul style=\"min-height:1.5em\"><li><p style=\"min-height:1.5em\">Provide insight and strategic recommendations on how Float can best serve our customers, from social proof to feature enhancements.</p></li><li><p style=\"min-height:1.5em\">Partner with internal teams to leverage customer feedback for product development and operational improvements.</p></li><li><p style=\"min-height:1.5em\">Help accelerate learning cycles by engaging customers who share our passion for simplifying corporate spending.</p></li><li><p style=\"min-height:1.5em\">Collaborate on initiatives that impact Float’s customers, from onboarding programs to strategic campaigns that drive engagement and growth.</p></li><li><p style=\"min-height:1.5em\">Support the development and execution of scalable processes that enhance the customer experience at every stage of their journey.</p></li></ul><p style=\"min-height:1.5em\"></p><p style=\"min-height:1.5em\"><strong>About You</strong></p><h3><strong>Here’s what sets you up for success at Float:</strong></h3><ul style=\"min-height:1.5em\"><li><p style=\"min-height:1.5em\"><strong>You Put Customers First, Always.</strong> You care deeply about delivering meaningful value. This may include AI-assisted scheduling and candidate communications, and AI-generated interview notes, guides or summaries to help our team focus on the conversation. All hiring decisions are made by our hiring team.</p><p style=\"min-height:1.5em\"></p><h2><strong>About the Role</strong></h2><p style=\"min-height:1.5em\">This is Float's first dedicated data engineering hire. You'll own the Snowflake architecture and ingestion layer end-to-end — the plumbing that carries data from banking partners, card processors, CRM, marketing platforms, and product systems into one clean, reliable, well-governed place.</p><p style=\"min-height:1.5em\"></p><p style=\"min-height:1.5em\">You'll work closely with our Analytics Engineer, who owns the dbt and transformation layer, and be the infrastructure backbone our Data Scientists and growing analytics team depend on. Together, you and the Analytics Engineer form the core of a data platform the rest of Float can trust and build on.</p><p style=\"min-height:1.5em\"></p><p style=\"min-height:1.5em\">We're at an inflection point. Growing transaction volumes and an expanding product surface mean there's real work to do — and you'll have the scope and ownership to do it properly.</p><p style=\"min-height:1.5em\"></p><h2><strong>What You'll Be Doing</strong></h2><ul style=\"min-height:1.5em\"><li><p style=\"min-height:1.5em\">Own Float's Snowflake architecture end-to-end — organization, cost efficiency, and access controls</p></li><li><p style=\"min-height:1.5em\">Design and build a real orchestration layer for our ingestion pipelines, replacing ad hoc processes</p></li><li><p style=\"min-height:1.5em\">Stand up observability and alerting so pipeline failures and data staleness are caught immediately, not downstream</p></li><li><p style=\"min-height:1.5em\">Introduce data contracts between producer and consumer systems, so upstream changes (new payment rails, new banking products, vendor field changes) stop silently breaking things</p></li><li><p style=\"min-height:1.5em\">Own the data reliability layer — establish CI/CD pipelines for data code, build data quality checks directly into pipelines, and orchestrate jobs that live outside of ingestion and dbt (ML pipelines, data quality runs, operational workflows), so everything is tested, automated, and deployed consistently</p></li><li><p style=\"min-height:1.5em\">Partner closely with our Analytics Engineer to keep the ingestion → transformation handoff clean and dependable — and collaborate on lineage tracking and metadata tooling so the broader team has visibility into where data comes from and how it flows</p></li><li><p style=\"min-height:1.5em\">Develop, document and socialize a target-state data architecture and phased migration roadmap, in partnership with data and engineering leadership.</p></li><li><p style=\"min-height:1.5em\">Build and maintain the data pipelines that power ML model training and inference — ensuring the data science team has reliable, well-structured feature data for ML use cases</p></li><li><p style=\"min-height:1.5em\">Leverage AI tooling across the full engineering lifecycle — from writing and reviewing pipeline code to accelerating observability, anomaly detection, and incident triage</p></li><li><p style=\"min-height:1.5em\">Partner with product and infrastructure engineering to maintain consistent telemetry standards across Float's codebases, ensuring product events flow reliably into the data platform.</p></li></ul><p style=\"min-height:1.5em\"></p><h2><strong>What Success Looks Like (6–12 Months)</strong></h2><p style=\"min-height:1.5em\">In your first 30 days, you're not building — you're mapping. You'll talk to the Analytics Engineer, the data scientists, and engineering stakeholders to understand what exists and what's broken — but also to finance, ops, and product teams to understand where data is and isn't being trusted across the business.</p><p style=\"min-height:1.5em\"></p><p style=\"min-height:1.5em\">By 60 days, you've stabilized the most urgent issues and produced a draft target architecture and prioritized roadmap — signed off with data and engineering leadership.</p><p style=\"min-height:1.5em\"></p><p style=\"min-height:1.5em\">By 90 days, you're executing: an orchestration layer, observability and alerting, and initial data quality checks on the most critical pipelines are in place.</p><p style=\"min-height:1.5em\"></p><p style=\"min-height:1.5em\">Longer term, success looks like:</p><ul style=\"min-height:1.5em\"><li><p style=\"min-height:1.5em\">Data the business trusts — analysts, data scientists, and stakeholders make decisions with confidence</p></li><li><p style=\"min-height:1.5em\">Pipelines with defined SLAs, clear ownership, and no silent failures</p></li><li><p style=\"min-height:1.5em\">A Snowflake environment that's intentional and cost-controlled</p></li><li><p style=\"min-height:1.5em\">Data contracts covering the large majority of critical sources, with a clear registry of what's covered</p></li><li><p style=\"min-height:1.5em\">An analytics engineering and data science team that's unblocked — focused on modeling and insight</p></li><li><p style=\"min-height:1.5em\">Infrastructure that scales with Float's next product launch</p></li></ul><p style=\"min-height:1.5em\"></p><h2><strong>What We're Looking For</strong></h2><ul style=\"min-height:1.5em\"><li><p style=\"min-height:1.5em\">Genuine proficiency in Python and SQL — not just functional, but strong</p></li><li><p style=\"min-height:1.5em\">Hands-on experience building and owning ELT/ETL pipelines at scale</p></li><li><p style=\"min-height:1.5em\">Deep experience with a modern cloud data platform (Snowflake, Databricks, or equivalent), including architecture, cost optimization, and access controls</p></li><li><p style=\"min-height:1.5em\">Real orchestration experience and a clear point of view on how to use it well</p></li><li><p style=\"min-height:1.5em\">dbt fluency — you won't own the transformation layer, but you'll work seamlessly with the person who does</p></li><li><p style=\"min-height:1.5em\">Practical experience implementing data observability, data quality frameworks, and data contracts — not environment</p></li><li><p style=\"min-height:1.5em\">You communicate clearly with non-technical stakeholders, earn trust across a business, and hold your technical opinions strongly but loosely</p></li><li><p style=\"min-height:1.5em\">You use AI tooling deliberately and daily — for coding, for monitoring, and for triage — and you have a clear point of view on where it genuinely behaves</p></li></ul></li></ul><p style=\"min-height:1.5em\">You'll thrive here if you're energized by ambiguity, default to action, hold strong opinions loosely, and take real pride in building All hiring decisions are made by our hiring team.\n\n\n\n\nABOUT THE ROLE\n\nThis is Float's first dedicated data engineering hire. You'll own the Snowflake architecture and ingestion layer end-to-end — the plumbing that carries data from banking partners, card processors, CRM, marketing platforms, and product systems into one clean, reliable, well-governed place.\n\n\n\nYou'll work closely with our Analytics Engineer, who owns the dbt and transformation layer, and be the infrastructure backbone our Data Scientists and growing analytics team depend on. Together, you and the Analytics Engineer form the core of a data platform the rest of Float can trust and build on.\n\n\n\nWe're at an inflection point. Growing transaction volumes and an expanding product surface mean there's real work to do — and you'll have the scope and ownership to do it properly.\n\n\n\n\nWHAT YOU'LL BE DOING\n\n - Own Float's Snowflake architecture end-to-end — organization, cost efficiency, and access controls\n\n - Design and build a real orchestration layer for our ingestion pipelines, replacing ad hoc processes\n\n - Stand up observability and alerting so pipeline failures and data staleness are caught immediately, not downstream\n\n - Introduce data contracts between producer and consumer systems, so upstream changes (new payment rails, new banking products, vendor field changes) stop silently breaking things\n\n - Own the data reliability layer — establish CI/CD pipelines for data code, build data quality checks directly into pipelines, and orchestrate jobs that live outside of ingestion and dbt (ML pipelines, data quality runs, operational workflows), so everything is tested, automated, and deployed consistently\n\n - Partner closely with our Analytics Engineer to keep the ingestion → transformation handoff clean and dependable — and collaborate on lineage tracking and metadata tooling so the broader team has visibility into where data comes from and how it flows\n\n - Develop, document and socialize a target-state data architecture and phased migration roadmap, in partnership with data and engineering leadership.\n\n - Build and maintain the data pipelines that power ML model training and inference — ensuring the data science team has reliable, well-structured feature data for ML use cases\n\n - Leverage AI tooling across the full engineering lifecycle — from writing and reviewing pipeline code to accelerating observability, anomaly detection, and incident triage\n\n - Partner with product and infrastructure engineering to maintain consistent telemetry standards across Float's codebases, ensuring product events flow reliably into the data platform.\n\n\n\n\nWHAT SUCCESS LOOKS LIKE (6–12 MONTHS)\n\nIn your first 30 days, you're not building — you're mapping. You'll talk to the Analytics Engineer, the data scientists, and engineering stakeholders to understand what exists and what's broken — but also to finance, ops, and product teams to understand where data is and isn't being trusted across the business.\n\n\n\nBy 60 days, you've stabilized the most urgent issues and produced a draft target architecture and prioritized roadmap — signed off with data and engineering leadership.\n\n\n\nBy 90 days, you're executing: an orchestration layer, observability and alerting, and initial data quality checks on the most critical pipelines are in place.\n\n\n\nLonger term, success looks like:\n\n - Data the business trusts — analysts, data scientists, and stakeholders make decisions with confidence\n\n - Pipelines with defined SLAs, clear ownership, and no silent failures\n\n - A Snowflake environment that's intentional and cost-controlled\n\n - Data contracts covering the large majority of critical sources, with a clear registry of what's covered\n\n - An analytics engineering and data science team that's unblocked — focused on modeling and insight\n\n - Infrastructure that scales with Float's next product launch\n\n\n\n\nWHAT WE'RE LOOKING FOR\n\n - Genuine proficiency in Python and SQL — not just functional, but strong\n\n - Hands-on experience building and owning ELT/ETL pipelines at scale\n\n - Deep experience with a modern cloud data platform (Snowflake, Databricks, or equivalent), including architecture, cost optimization, and access controls\n\n - Real orchestration experience and a clear point of view on how to use it well\n\n - dbt fluency — you won't own the transformation layer, but you'll work seamlessly with the person who does\n\n - Practical experience implementing data observability, data quality frameworks, and data contracts — not just familiarity with the concepts, but having actually put them in place\n\n - A track record of looking at a messy data environment and developing a clear, pragmatic point of view on what good looks like — and how to get there without over-engineering\n\n - You've built something from scratch in a high-ownership environment\n\n - You communicate clearly with non-technical stakeholders, earn trust across a business, and hold your technical opinions strongly but loosely\n\n - You use AI tooling deliberately and daily — for coding, for monitoring, and for triage — and you have a clear point of view on where it genuinely accelerates your work and where it doesn't\n\n - Nice to Haves:\n   \n   - Experience with data governance and compliance in a regulated environment\n   \n   - Fintech or payments background — understanding how transaction, card, and banking data behaves\n\nYou'll thrive here if you're energized by ambiguity, default to action, hold strong opinions loosely, and take real pride in building things properly. Budgets and reporting are not adoption goals in themselves. They exist to make a controller confident enough to raise a limit, open a new spend category, or migrate a spend type onto card — and that confidence is what shows up as revenue. Using AI first approach to bring in budget visibility into the product and meeting users where they're at; you're objective will be to automate away the friction of finance reconciliation through automations, integrations and building out a delightful scaled spend experience. </p><p style=\"min-height:1.5em\">You’ll work with a designer and four engineers, alongside Product Ops/Analytics, and partner closely with Accounting, CX, and Sales.</p><p style=\"min-height:1.5em\"></p><h2><strong>What You’ll Own</strong></h2><h3><strong>Surface area</strong></h3><ul style=\"min-height:1.5em\"><strong>Spend programs and controls</strong> — policy definition and enforcement, the container binding policy, budget, and card</p></li><li><p style=\"min-height:1.5em\"><strong>Reporting</strong> — the reporting platform, period comparison, out-of-policy spend visibility, and the reporting views that surface on users command center</p></li><li><p style=\"min-height:1.5em\"><strong>AI enabled reporting </strong>- Incorporating AI to help answer finance questions based on users spend data</p></li><li><p mid-market accounts</p></li><li><p style=\"min-height:1.5em\">The behavioural link between them: do accounts that adopt budgets actually raise ceilings and open categories?</p></li></ul><p Budgets and reporting are not adoption goals in themselves. They exist to make a controller confident enough to raise a limit, open a new spend category, or migrate a spend type onto card — and that confidence is what shows up as revenue. Using AI first approach to bring in budget visibility into the product and meeting users where they're at; you're objective will be to automate away the friction of finance reconciliation through automations, integrations and building out a delightful scaled spend experience. \n\nYou’ll work with a designer and four engineers, alongside Product Ops/Analytics, and partner closely with Accounting, CX, and Sales.\n\n\n\n\nWHAT YOU’LL OWN\n\n\nSURFACE AREA\n\n - Budgets — funding pools, categorization, recurring structures, enforcement\n\n - Spend programs and controls — policy definition and enforcement, the container binding policy, budget, and card\n\n - Reporting — the reporting platform, period comparison, out-of-policy spend visibility, and the reporting views that surface on users command center\n\n - AI enabled reporting - Incorporating AI to help answer finance questions based on users spend data\n\n - Month end reconciliation automation - AI first month end workflows to automate transaction coding \n\n\nOUTCOMES YOU’RE ACCOUNTABLE FOR\n\n - Spend per account\n\n - Budget and reporting adoption across mid-market accounts\n\n - The behavioural link between them: do accounts that adopt budgets actually raise ceilings and open categories?\n\n\n\n\nWHAT YOU’LL BE RESPONSIBLE FOR\n\n\nPRODUCT STRATEGY AND ROADMAP\n\n - Own the squad’s roadmap end-to-end: sizing, sequencing, and cuts. Candidate initiatives are pre-populated; the judgment about what ships and in what order is yours.\n\n - Make the trade-off calls on the pillar’s most constrained roadmap, and escalate with options when scope and capacity don’t reconcile.\n\n - Benchmark against Ramp and the broader spend management market, and be specific about which gaps are worth closing and which aren’t.\n\n\nPRODUCT EXECUTION AND DELIVERY\n\n - Take features from discovery through launch and iteration with a designer and four engineers.\n\n - Write requirements that engineering can estimate against, in plain language rather than implementation jargon.\n\n - Manage dependencies across squads — you consume detection, notification delivery, and approvals routing as services from another squad, and you supply policy definitions that a third squad evaluates at transaction time.\n\n\nANALYTICS AND INSTRUMENTATION\n\n - Define the instrumentation that doesn’t exist yet, including limit-ceiling change events attributed to budget adoption, and category expansion events.\n\n - Set baselines with Product Ops in your first weeks and hold the line on measuring behaviour change, not just adoption.\n\n - Be willing to conclude that a thesis you inherited is wrong, and say so.\n\n\nCUSTOMER-FOCUSED DEVELOPMENT\n\n - Work directly with finance leaders and controllers, and with Sales and CX, to understand where control and visibility break down.\n\n - Reduce friction in high-complexity B2B workflows — permissions, policy configuration, bulk operations, reporting exports, accounting integrations.\n\n\nAI-ENABLED PRODUCT AND WORKFLOW THINKING\n\n - Use AI tools to accelerate research, documentation, analysis, and planning.\n\n - Identify high-leverage, responsible AI use cases in reporting and analysis — natural-language querying over spend data is on the roadmap — and evaluate risks, data requirements, and guardrails when proposing them.\n\n\n\n\nWHAT SUCCESS LOOKS LIKE (6–12 MONTHS)\n\n - You’ve shipped budgets and a phased reporting rollout, with real adoption in mid-market accounts.\n\n - Spend per active card is up, and you can explain which of your initiatives moved it.\n\n - The visibility-drives-spend thesis is either evidenced or disproven, and the roadmap reflects the answer.\n\n - Established-cardholder decline recovery is measurably better.\n\n - Engineering, Design, and Analytics want to work on your squad, and leadership trusts your prioritization without needing to re-derive it.\n\n\n\n\nWHAT WE’RE LOOKING FOR\n\n - You have strong product fundamentals. 5+ years of hands-on B2B SaaS product management in a startup or scale-up, with end-to-end ownership of a meaningful surface and measurable impact to show for it.\n\n - You’re analytically strong. Comfortable with SQL or a genuine working partnership with data teams. You define your own metrics, spot when a number is measuring the wrong thing, and change your mind when the evidence is clear.\n\n - You act like an owner. You take responsibility for outcomes, not output. You escalate risks with options attached.\n\n - You have conviction. You can hold a position through pushback when you have evidence, and drop it quickly when you don’t.\n\n - You have good product judgment. You can tell good design from bad, you think in workflows and edge cases, and you can navigate a domain where the edge cases have accounting consequences.\n\n - You put customers first. You start from real workflow friction, and you can distinguish a genuinely painful workflow from a merely unfamiliar one.\n\n - You’re curious about AI. You use modern tools to sharpen your own output, and you’re open-minded about where AI belongs in the product.\n\n - Nice to haves: \n   \n   - Fintech, spend management, or financial operations product experience\n   \n   - Exposure to policy engines, permissions systems, budgeting or FP&A tools, or reporting and analytics platforms\n   \n   - Familiarity with accounting workflows — GL structures, dimensions, month-end close\n\n\n\n\nTHIS ROLE MAY NOT BE A FIT IF\n\n - You want a well-instrumented problem space with clean baselines waiting for you.\n\n - You prefer executing a roadmap someone else has sequenced.\n\n - You’re uncomfortable owning a number you can only move indirectly, through someone else’s behaviour change.\n\n - You avoid analytical work, or treat metric definition as someone else’s job.\n\n\n\n\nFLEXIBLE WORK MODEL\n\nFloat is Toronto-based with a hybrid model: in-office collaboration days, plus occasional in-person time for workflow-discovery sessions. Remote candidates within Canada considered, with occasional travel to Toronto.\n\n\n\n\nOUR HIRING PHILOSOPHY\n\nWe hire for character, curiosity, and learning velocity before credentials. All hiring decisions are made by our hiring team.</p><p style=\"min-height:1.5em\"></p><h2><strong>About the Role</strong></h2><p style=\"min-height:1.5em\">We're looking for a Customer Activation Team Manager to lead a team of five Customer Activation Managers (CAMs) who own one of the most important handoffs in our business: the moment a deal closes and a new customer needs to get up and running. Once an Account Executive closes a deal, the Customer Activation team takes over — training spenders, migrating corporate card spend, and onboarding customers across Float's full product suite — owning the entire activation journey for a customer's first 120 days.</p><p style=\"min-height:1.5em\"></p><p style=\"min-height:1.5em\">This is a backfill for a strong team with solid foundations already in place, looking for a leader to build on that base. You'll work closely with Account Executives, Product, and Engineering to keep the activation motion running smoothly, standardize how the team operates, and ensure customers realize value fast. This role is hands-on: you'll run the team like a revenue organization against realized TPV and other revenue-tied metrics, and you won't be afraid to get into the weeds on individual accounts.</p><p style=\"min-height:1.5em\"></p><h2><strong>What You'll Do </strong></h2><ul style=\"min-height:1.5em\"><li><p style=\"min-height:1.5em\">Lead and develop a team of five Customer Activation Managers, owning their performance, growth, and day-to-day support — in person, in the Toronto office from Tuesdays to Thursdays.</p></li><li><p style=\"min-height:1.5em\">Own the team's results against realized TPV (total payment volume) and other revenue-tied activation metrics.</p></li><li><p style=\"min-height:1.5em\">Standardize onboarding playbooks across scenarios so customers get a consistent experience regardless of which CAM they work with.</p></li><li><p style=\"min-height:1.5em\">Build out playbooks, processes, and metrics for multi-product adoption beyond the first 30 days, extending focus across the full 120-day journey.</p></li><li><p style=\"min-height:1.5em\">Develop deep product fluency across Float's full payments suite — not just cards — and translate that understanding into how the team designs and runs the customer onboarding journey.</p></li><li><p style=\"min-height:1.5em\">Get into the weeds on individual accounts — diagnose blockers, unstick stalled activations, and coach CAMs through complex situations.</p></li><li><p style=\"min-height:1.5em\">Bring rigor and follow-up discipline to the team's sales-like motion, holding reps accountable for proactively driving accounts to activation.</p></li><li><p style=\"min-height:1.5em\">Flag account risks early and proactively — to CAMs, Sales, Customer Success, and Leadership — before they threaten activation or retention.</p></li><li><p style=\"min-height:1.5em\">Partner with Sales to understand the customer journey from first interaction through the CAM hand-off, and with Customer Success to ensure a smooth transition into long-term adoption beyond the first 120 days.</p></li><li><p style=\"min-height:1.5em\">Represent the Customer Activation team in front of customers directly for high-value accounts, including presenting to stakeholders.</p></li><li><p style=\"min-height:1.5em\">Surface product and process feedback to Product and Engineering leadership, using CAM and customer input to drive real changes to the activation experience.</p></li><li><p style=\"min-height:1.5em\">Advocate cross-functionally with Product, Engineering, and Marketing to remove friction from the activation journey.</p></li><li><p style=\"min-height:1.5em\">Build a team culture where CAMs feel supported, recognized, and set up to do their best work.</p></li></ul><p Once an Account Executive closes a deal, the Customer Activation team takes over — training spenders, migrating corporate card spend, and onboarding customers across Float's full product suite — owning the entire activation journey for a customer's first 120 days.\n\n\n\nThis is a backfill for a strong team with solid foundations already in place, looking for a leader to build on that base. You'll work closely with Account Executives, Product, and Engineering to keep the activation motion running smoothly, standardize how the team operates, and ensure customers realize value fast. This role is hands-on: you'll run the team like a revenue organization against realized TPV and other revenue-tied metrics, and you won't be afraid to get into the weeds on individual accounts.\n\n\n\n\nWHAT YOU'LL DO \n\n - Lead and develop a team of five Customer Activation Managers, owning their performance, growth, and day-to-day support — in person, in the Toronto office from Tuesdays to Thursdays.\n\n - Own the team's results against realized TPV (total payment volume) and other revenue-tied activation metrics.\n\n - Standardize onboarding playbooks across scenarios so customers get a consistent experience regardless of which CAM they work with.\n\n - Build out playbooks, processes, and metrics for multi-product adoption beyond the first 30 days, extending focus across the full 120-day journey.\n\n - Develop deep product fluency across Float's full payments suite — not just cards — and translate that understanding into how the team designs and runs the customer onboarding journey.\n\n - Get into the weeds on individual accounts — diagnose blockers, unstick stalled activations, and coach CAMs through complex situations.\n\n - Bring rigor and follow-up discipline to the team's sales-like motion, holding reps accountable for proactively driving accounts to activation.\n\n - Flag account risks early and proactively — to CAMs, Sales, Customer Success, and Leadership — before they threaten activation or retention.\n\n - Partner with Sales to understand the customer journey from first interaction through the CAM hand-off, and with Customer Success to ensure a smooth transition into long-term adoption beyond the first 120 days.\n\n - Represent the Customer Activation team in front of customers directly for high-value accounts, including presenting to stakeholders.\n\n - Surface product and process feedback to Product and Engineering leadership, using CAM and customer input to drive real changes to the activation experience.\n\n - Fraud detection, AML compliance, payments operations, and dispute resolution already run on this decisioning backbone today. What’s missing is a single owner. </p><p style=\"min-height:1.5em\"></p><p style=\"min-height:1.5em\">As the founding Product Manager for Credit &amp; Risk Engineering, you’ll turn this shared decisioning and monitoring layer into a truly owned product: fast, accurate, and relentlessly efficient as volume scales. You’ll sit at the intersection of Float’s credit roadmap and growth funnel, sequencing a small engineering team across real infrastructure debt and a flagship new build — the FlexLine decisioning engine — while ensuring the systems you own keep Float’s day-to-day risk operations safe and scalable.</p><p style=\"min-height:1.5em\"></p><h2><strong>What You'll Do</strong></h2><ul style=\"min-height:1.5em\"><li><p style=\"min-height:1.5em\">Own the roadmap and sequencing for the Credit &amp; Risk Engineering squad across three domains — starting with the trade-off between paying down risk infrastructure debt and building the FlexLine decisioning engine.</p></li><li><p style=\"min-height:1.5em\">Own the decisioning and automation systems that drive KYB/KYC approval speed and accuracy, delivered so Float's risk operations team can hit its approval-time targets.</p></li><li><p style=\"min-height:1.5em\">Own the tooling behind fraud detection, AML compliance, payments operations, and dispute resolution — daily infrastructure the company already depends on.</p></li><li><p style=\"min-height:1.5em\">Own risk decision operating cost per account as your team's primary efficiency metric, proving the systems scale without proportional headcount growth.</p></li><li><p style=\"min-height:1.5em\">Own the in-app credit experiences — applying for credit, viewing balances and limits, setting up repayments — and their target speed, in support of Float's credit product roadmap.</p></li><li><p style=\"min-height:1.5em\">Be the standing source of truth on where the credit product roadmap ends and credit-engineering scope begins, in ongoing partnership with the GM of Credit.</p></li></ul><p style=\"min-height:1.5em\"></p><h2><strong>About You</strong></h2><h3>Here's what sets you up for success at Float:</h3><ul style=\"min-height:1.5em\"><li><p style=\"min-height:1.5em\"><strong>You Put Customers First, Always.</strong> You care deeply about delivering meaningful value. Whether you're building internal systems or customer-facing features, you're always thinking about how to make life better for our users.</p></li><li><p style=\"min-height:1.5em\"><strong>You Act Like an Owner.</strong> You take responsibility for outcomes, step up to challenges, and seek solutions proactively—doing what's best for the business, not just your role.</p></li><li><p style=\"min-height:1.5em\"><strong>You Think Big and Move Fast.</strong> You're energized by building from 0 to 1. You're not afraid to challenge the status quo, experiment quickly, and learn as you go.</p></li><li><p style=\"min-height:1.5em\"><strong>You Constantly Learn and Grow.</strong> You're hungry to improve your craft and open to feedback. Trusted by more than 10,000 Canadian companies, Float provides high-limit corporate cards, automated expense management, next-day bill payments, high-yield accounts, and industry-leading support, all built in Canada, for Canada. Float recently announced our $85 million Series C https://floatfinancial.com/press/float-financial-raises-cad-85-million-series-c, and is backed by world-class investors, including Inovia Capital, Growth Equity at Goldman Sachs Alternatives, OMERS Ventures, and Silicon Valley Bank.\n\n \n\nOur team is a collection of ambitious, collaborative and mission-driven people from all walks of life but with one goal: helping Canadian companies not just survive but thrive. Fraud detection, AML compliance, payments operations, and dispute resolution already run on this decisioning backbone today. What’s missing is a single owner. \n\n\n\nAs the founding Product Manager for Credit & Risk Engineering, you’ll turn this shared decisioning and monitoring layer into a truly owned product: fast, accurate, and relentlessly efficient as volume scales. You’ll sit at the intersection of Float’s credit roadmap and growth funnel, sequencing a small engineering team across real infrastructure debt and a flagship new build — the FlexLine decisioning engine — while ensuring the systems you own keep Float’s day-to-day risk operations safe and scalable.\n\n\n\n\nWHAT YOU'LL DO\n\n - Own the roadmap and sequencing for the Credit & Risk Engineering squad across three domains — starting with the trade-off between paying down risk infrastructure debt and building the FlexLine decisioning engine.\n\n - Own the decisioning and automation systems that drive KYB/KYC approval speed and accuracy, delivered so Float's risk operations team can hit its approval-time targets.\n\n - Own the tooling behind fraud detection, AML compliance, payments operations, and dispute resolution — daily infrastructure the company already depends on.\n\n - Own risk decision operating cost per account as your team's primary efficiency metric, proving the systems scale without proportional headcount growth.\n\n - Own the in-app credit experiences — applying for credit, viewing balances and limits, setting up repayments — and their target speed, in support of Float's credit product roadmap.\n\n - Be the standing source of truth on where the credit product roadmap ends and credit-engineering scope begins, in ongoing partnership with the GM of Credit.\n\n\n\n\nABOUT YOU\n\n\nHERE'S WHAT SETS YOU UP FOR SUCCESS AT FLOAT:\n\n - You Put Customers First, Always. You take responsibility for outcomes, step up to challenges, and seek solutions proactively—doing what's best for the business, not just your role.\n\n - You Think Big and Move Fast. You're energized by building from 0 to 1. You're not afraid to challenge the status quo, experiment quickly, and learn as you go.\n\n - You Constantly Learn and Grow. You're hungry to improve your craft and open to feedback. You bring a growth mindset to everything you do.\n\n - You Raise the Bar. You care about doing things well and efficiently. You balance speed with rigor and always look for ways to improve how we work.\n\n - You Win as a Team. You're a generous collaborator who values communication, context, and shared wins. You lift others up and help make the team stronger.\n\n\n\n\nWHAT YOU'LL BRING:\n\n - 5+ years of product management experience, with meaningful time personally owning a credit underwriting or risk-decisioning outcome — not just supporting one.\n\n - A track record building and owning infrastructure or internal-tooling products where another team, not an end customer, is who you're building for.\n\n - Real comfort operating inside compliance-heavy domains — KYB/KYC, transaction monitoring, fraud, AML, payments operations, or disputes.\n\n - An automation-first instinct: your default question is how a decision becomes automatic, not what the screen looks like.\n\n - Experience sequencing a roadmap under real capacity constraints, including saying no to work that looked mandatory.\n\n - Comfort negotiating and holding scope boundaries with senior, opinionated stakeholders you don't manage.\n\n\n\n\nTHIS MAY NOT BE THE ROLE FOR YOU IF:\n\n - You want to spend most of your time on customer-facing product experiences — this role is almost entirely about the systems behind them.\n\n - You're energized by visible launches and find debt-paydown or \"keep the lights on\" work unrewarding — the first phase here is deliberately about stabilizing existing systems before new build.\n\n - You want one clear manager and one roadmap — this seat drives outcomes for three separate leaders (credit, growth, and risk operations) who each own a piece of the result.\n\n\n\n\nFLEXIBLE WORK MODEL\n\nFloat is Toronto-based with a hybrid model: in-office collaboration days, plus occasional in-person time for workflow-discovery sessions. It's a hands-on, executional role built for someone who lives and breathes conversion rate optimization, with a direct line to shaping how a fast-growing fintech turns visitors into pipeline.\n\n\n\nWHAT YOU'LL BE RESPONSIBLE FOR\n\n - Own the web CRO roadmap end to end: build and prioritize a testing plan, run experiments, and report on lift against clear win/loss criteria\n\n - Build and iterate landing pages by segment and vertical, and lead the post-launch optimization of our new website, refreshing copy and improving the customer journey so more visitors convert\n\n - Design and own self-serve and AE-led site journeys, including the handoff logic to product and sales, in partnership with our Product Growth team\n\n - Define and refine where and how visitors route between self-serve and AE-led motions, so the highest-value opportunities get the right intervention at the right time\n\n - Own lower-funnel demand capture, working with XDR to set clear MQL/SAO criteria and handoff SLAs\n\n - Partner with RevOps on CRO-relevant reporting and testing frameworks; RevOps owns the attribution model, you own turning it into a prioritized testing plan\n\n - Bring rigor to experimentation: sound test design, clear hypotheses, and honest reads on statistical significance, not just \"ran a test\"\n\n\nWHAT YOU'LL BRING\n\n - 5+ years of hands-on CRO or web optimization ownership at a high-growth company, with real, personal accountability for conversion outcomes, not just contribution to them\n\n - Deep comfort with Webflow (or a similar site platform), A/B testing tools, and analytics/heatmapping tools; you can set up and run a test without waiting on engineering\n\n - A track record of designing customer journeys across different segments or motions (e.g., self-serve vs. sales-assisted), and making the routing/handoff logic work in practice, not just on a whiteboard\n\n - Strong analytical instincts: you can size a test, read a result honestly, and know when a \"win\" isn't actually significant\n\n - Experience partnering with product, sales, and ops teams to ship changes to a live site without breaking things for other teams' priorities (e.g., SEO)\n\n - Genuine comfort with ambiguity and a fixed capacity constraint — you're used to prioritizing ruthlessly against limited design/dev resources\n\n - Practical, day-to-day use of AI tools to move faster on research, insight synthesis, and experimentation\n\n\nTHIS MAY NOT BE THE ROLE FOR YOU IF\n\n - You want to own campaign strategy or channel mix rather than the conversion layer of the funnel\n\n - You've mostly directed CRO work rather than building and shipping it yourself\n\n - You need a fixed roadmap and are uncomfortable when priorities shift mid-quarter\n\n - You prefer to stay at the strategy layer rather than being deeply hands-on in a site builder\n\n - You like to run the same CRO playbook everyone else uses\n\n - You haven't meaningfully integrated AI into how you work\n\n\nABOUT YOU\n\nHere's what sets you up for success at Float:\n\n - You Put Customers First, Always. You care deeply about delivering meaningful value. Whether you're building internal systems or customer-facing features, you're always thinking about how to make life better for our users.\n\n - You Act Like an Owner. You take responsibility for outcomes, step up to challenges, and seek solutions proactively—doing what's best for the business, not just your role.\n\n - You Think Big and Move Fast. You're energized by building from 0 to 1. You're not afraid to challenge the status quo, experiment quickly, and learn as you go.\n\n - You Constantly Learn and Grow. You're hungry to improve your craft and open to feedback. You bring a growth mindset to everything you do.\n\n - You Raise the Bar. You care about doing things well and efficiently. You balance speed with rigour and always look for ways to improve how we work.\n\n - You Win as a Team. You're a generous collaborator who values communication, context, and shared wins. You lift others up and help make the team stronger.\n\n\nOUR HIRING PHILOSOPHY\n\nWe hire for character, curiosity, and learning velocity before credentials. Today, too many mid-market accounts sign with Float and then sit at a fraction of the employee coverage they should have — because issuing cards is manual, onboarding is manual, and nothing tells an admin who is missing a card.</p><p style=\"min-height:1.5em\"></p><p style=\"min-height:1.5em\">Your job is to remove every manual step between “an employee exists” and “that employee has spent.” You’ll own <strong>active cardholder penetration</strong> — the share of employees at each account holding and actively using a Float card. It’s one of two terms that multiply into Float’s card volume, and it’s yours alone.</p><p style=\"min-height:1.5em\"></p><p style=\"min-height:1.5em\">This is a role for a PM with solid fundamentals who wants to own a real number with real scope, alongside senior product leaders. Through our innovative platform, Float enables businesses to streamline financial operations and optimize cash flow, so they can focus on what matters most: growth. \n\n \n\nAs one of Canada’s fastest growing companies https://www.theglobeandmail.com/business/rob-magazine/top-growing-companies/article-ranking-canadas-top-growing-companies-of-2024/ and top-rated startups in 2025 https://www.linkedin.com/posts/floatfinancial_were-proud-to-share-that-float-has-been-activity-7387093684720300032-2DDz/, 2024 https://www.linkedin.com/pulse/linkedin-top-startups-2024-15-canadian-companies-rise-linkedin-news-llihe/ and 2023 https://lnkd.in/TSU23CA, Float is customer-obsessed, passionate and entrepreneurial, with a team that includes leaders from Uber, Stripe, Shopify, Top Hat, Ada, Doordash, Snowflake, and Wealthsimple.\n\n \n\nAt Float, everyone is an owner, bringing their unique perspective to our team and product. Your voice is important, and we take having a culture based on feedback seriously. We openly share our thoughts and differing opinions so we can continue to improve. We do our best to keep our decision-making decentralized so that all team members feel ownership in our success.\n\n \n\n\nOUR PRODUCT\n\nFloat is Canada’s intelligent financial operating system, combining modern financial services and software to help businesses spend, save, and grow. Trusted by more than 10,000 Canadian companies, Float provides high-limit corporate cards, automated expense management, next-day bill payments, high-yield accounts, and industry-leading support, all built in Canada, for Canada. Float recently announced our $85 million Series C https://floatfinancial.com/press/float-financial-raises-cad-85-million-series-c, and is backed by world-class investors, including Inovia Capital, Growth Equity at Goldman Sachs Alternatives, OMERS Ventures, and Silicon Valley Bank.\n\n \n\nOur team is a collection of ambitious, collaborative and mission-driven people from all walks of life but with one goal: helping Canadian companies not just survive but thrive. And we’re looking for bold innovators to help shape the future of business finance in Canada.\n\n\n\n\nAI USE IN OUR HIRING PROCESS\n\nWe use technology, including artificial intelligence (AI), to support parts of our hiring process. This may include AI-assisted scheduling and candidate communications, and AI-generated interview notes, guides or summaries to help our team focus on the conversation. All hiring decisions are made by our hiring team.\n\n\n\n\nABOUT THE ROLE\n\nWe’re hiring a Product Manager for our Mid-Market Activation squad — one of three squads inside Float’s Spend Management pillar, reporting to the Head of Spend Management.\n\n\n\nThe mission is simple to state and hard to do: put a Float card in the hands of every employee who should have one, and get them spending fast. Today, too many mid-market accounts sign with Float and then sit at a fraction of the employee coverage they should have — because issuing cards is manual, onboarding is manual, and nothing tells an admin who is missing a card.\n\n\n\nYour job is to remove every manual step between “an employee exists” and “that employee has spent.” You’ll own active cardholder penetration — the share of employees at each account holding and actively using a Float card. It’s one of two terms that multiply into Float’s card volume, and it’s yours alone.\n\n\n\nThis is a role for a PM with solid fundamentals who wants to own a real number with real scope, alongside senior product leaders. You’ll work with a designer and four engineers, plus Product Ops/Analytics, Sales, and CX.\n\n\n\n\nWHAT YOU’LL OWN\n\n\nSURFACE AREA\n\n - Card issuance and provisioning — templates, bulk create, and the workflows admins use to get cards out\n\n - HRIS and SCIM integrations — new hire in the HR system triggers a card, with no admin action\n\n - The Overview page and Action Items — the surface that tells an admin what to do next, plus the framework other squads publish their items into\n\n - Onboarding and activation nudges — everything between card issued and first successful transaction\n\n - Reimbursement-to-card conversion — turning out-of-pocket spend into a signal for who needs a card\n\n - Activation-window declines — first-transaction failures on brand new cards, which are usually a configuration problem at issuance rather than a limit problem\n\n\nOUTCOMES YOU’RE ACCOUNTABLE FOR\n\n - Active cardholder penetration\n\n - Median time to first spend for a new cardholder\n\n - Share of mid-market accounts with a live HRIS/SCIM connection\n\n - Share of new cards issued through automated provisioning rather than manual create\n\n\n\n\nWHAT YOU’LL BE RESPONSIBLE FOR\n\n\nPRODUCT EXECUTION AND DELIVERY\n\n - Own features end-to-end, from discovery through launch and iteration.\n\n - Translate customer and business problems into clear requirements and user stories that engineering can estimate against.\n\n - Partner closely with Design and Engineering to ship intuitive, high-quality workflows on time.\n\n - Manage dependencies, scope trade-offs, and delivery risks with clarity and accountability.\n\n\nROADMAP OWNERSHIP\n\n - Own your squad’s roadmap within a defined mission and metric. Candidate initiatives are pre-populated; sizing, sequencing, and cuts are your call, with support from the Head of Spend Management.\n\n - Defend that sequencing in pillar prioritization conversations, with trade-offs and impact stated plainly.\n\n - Balance speed, quality, and commercial priorities within your scope, and re-cut the plan when the data says the current one is wrong.\n\n\nCUSTOMER-FOCUSED DEVELOPMENT\n\n - Talk to admins, HR, and ops teams — the people doing the provisioning — and to Sales and CX about where accounts stall.\n\n - Identify and remove high-friction steps in B2B workflows: permissions, bulk actions, integrations, onboarding.\n\n\nDATA-DRIVEN DECISION MAKING\n\n - Define and track success metrics for everything you ship.\n\n - Set baselines with Product Ops early, and instrument Action Item completion, which doesn’t exist today.\n\n - Analyze funnels and experiments to guide iteration, and improve measurement clarity in your area.\n\n\nAI-ENABLED PRODUCT AND WORKFLOW THINKING\n\n - Use AI tools to accelerate research, documentation, analysis, and planning.\n\n - Identify responsible, high-leverage AI use cases in provisioning and activation, and evaluate risks, data requirements, and guardrails when proposing them.\n\n\n\n\nWHAT SUCCESS LOOKS LIKE (6–12 MONTHS)\n\n - You independently own and deliver against your squad’s roadmap with minimal day-to-day direction.\n\n - Active cardholder penetration is measurably up at mid-market accounts, and automated provisioning has displaced a meaningful share of manual card creation.\n\n - Time to first spend is down, and first-transaction declines on new cards are down.\n\n - Action Item completion is instrumented, baselined, and improving.\n\n - You’re seen as a reliable, coachable, high-growth PM who consistently raises the bar.\n\n\n\n\nWHAT WE’RE LOOKING FOR\n\n - You have strong product fundamentals. 3+ years of hands-on B2B SaaS product management in a startup or scale-up. You’ve owned features end-to-end and can point to measurable impact.\n\n - You put customers first. You start from real workflow friction and care deeply about usability. You can tell a high-friction B2B workflow from a low-friction one.\n\n - You act like an owner. You take responsibility for outcomes, not output. You escalate risks with options and follow through on commitments.\n\n - You’re analytically strong. Comfortable with metrics, funnels, and experimentation, with SQL familiarity or a strong partnership with data teams. You use evidence to decide and change your mind when the data is clear.\n\n - You have good product judgment. You can differentiate good from bad design, you think in workflows and edge cases, and you partner well with Design and Engineering.\n\n - You’re coachable with a high growth slope. You seek feedback, learn quickly, and improve your craft. You’re resilient in ambiguity and energized by growth.\n\n - You’re curious about AI. You use modern tools to improve your productivity and clarity, and you’re open-minded about how AI can improve both the product and how PMs work.\n\n - Nice to have\n   \n   - Fintech, spend management, or financial operations product experience\n   \n   - SMB or mid-market focused B2B SaaS\n   \n   - Exposure to integrations (HRIS, SCIM, SSO), provisioning systems, permissions, or bulk operations\n   \n   - Experience with activation, onboarding, or growth-style product work\n\n\n\n\nTHIS ROLE MAY NOT BE A FIT IF\n\n - You prefer heavy direction rather than operating independently within a defined scope.\n\n - You struggle to connect product work to measurable outcomes.\n\n - You avoid analytical work, or decision-making based on data.\n\n - You resist new tools, feedback, or evolving workflows.\n\n\n\n\nFLEXIBLE WORK MODEL\n\nFloat is Toronto-based with a hybrid model: in-office collaboration days, plus occasional in-person time for workflow-discovery sessions. Remote candidates within Canada considered, with occasional travel to Toronto.\n\n\n\n\nOUR HIRING PHILOSOPHY\n\nWe hire for character, curiosity, and learning velocity before credentials. Titles matter less than impact, and every hire is expected to raise the bar for Float as a whole.\n\n\n\n\nWHY YOU SHOULD JOIN\n\n - Work at one of Canada's fastest-growing fintech companies\n\n - Make a real impact in a high-autonomy, high-growth role\n\n - Collaborate with an ambitious and supportive team\n\n - Competitive compensation, equity options, and benefits\n\n - Hybrid work model – we are based in Toronto with in-office days for connection and collaboration\n\n - Enjoy catered team lunches every Tuesday, Wednesday and Thursday\n\n - Bring your pup to our dog-friendly office\n\n - Thrive in a high-trust, high-performance culture where your work truly matters\n\n \n\n\nIN SHORT\n\nAt Float, you’ll thrive if you’re bold, curious, and eager to make a real impact. We're building something special—and having a lot of fun along the way. All hiring decisions are made by our hiring team.</p><p style=\"min-height:1.5em\"></p><h2><strong>About the Role</strong></h2><p style=\"min-height:1.5em\">Float is hiring a Founding Lead to own and accelerate Float Intelligence end to end, across the technical foundations, the data, and the product experiences, all under a single mandate. Float Intelligence is how we bring agentic AI finance to every business in Canada: a product that does the finance work our customers do by hand today, coding transactions, chasing receipts, checking spend against policy, and gathering invoices out of inboxes and vendor portals. We shipped the first version this year and it worked. Now we are building the rest of it, and we are building it fast.</p><p style=\"min-height:1.5em\"></p><p style=\"min-height:1.5em\">You would lead a small, fast-moving team of product engineers and data/ML engineers, reporting directly to the Head of Product. This is intentionally a hybrid seat across Engineering and Product leadership. You own the roadmap for what gets built, and you make the technical calls: model choice, evaluation, what has to be deterministic, and what a launch is gated on. The team ships into other product teams' surfaces and builds net-new surfaces that put AI directly in front of customers.</p><p style=\"min-height:1.5em\"></p><p style=\"min-height:1.5em\">This is a true end-to-end owner role. The people who do best here are ex-founders and highly capable technical leaders with strong commercial product taste, opinionated about both what to build and how to build it, and drawn to the highest-leverage, most cutting-edge AI work across Float's entire product surface.</p><p style=\"min-height:1.5em\"></p><h2><strong>What You'll Be Responsible For</strong></h2><ul style=\"min-height:1.5em\"><li><p style=\"min-height:1.5em\">Leading, growing, and developing a small team of product engineers and data/ML engineers.</p></li><li><p style=\"min-height:1.5em\">Owning the roadmap for Float's AI experiences alongside the Head of Product, including proposing new bets.</p></li><li><p style=\"min-height:1.5em\">Taking AI products from zero to one, from exploratory proofs of concept through to the experiences that reach customers at scale.</p></li><li><p style=\"min-height:1.5em\">Making the technical calls: model and LLM approach, evaluation design, and the infrastructure for scale, latency, and inference cost.</p></li><li><p style=\"min-height:1.5em\">Building the shared platform layer, where required for: extraction, evaluation, observability, agent and prompt frameworks, and data pipelines, that other product teams build on rather than rebuild.</p></li><li><p style=\"min-height:1.5em\">Equipping internal product teams with the AI models and engines they need to ship the experiences they want, and building new customer-facing surfaces that expose those experiences directly.</p></li><li><p style=\"min-height:1.5em\">Partnering with the product managers whose areas these experiences ship into, so each one lands well and ownership is clear afterward.</p></li><li><p style=\"min-height:1.5em\">Deciding what to stop, since exploratory work only pays off when the things that are not working get killed quickly.</p></li></ul><p style=\"min-height:1.5em\"></p><h2><strong>About You</strong></h2><h3><strong>Here's what sets you up for Whether you're building internal systems or customer-facing features, you're always thinking about how to make life better for our users.</p></li><li><p style=\"min-height:1.5em\"><strong>You Act Like an Owner.</strong> You take responsibility for outcomes, step up to challenges, and seek solutions proactively—doing what's best for the business, not just your role.</p></li><li><p style=\"min-height:1.5em\"><strong>You Think Big and Move Fast.</strong> You're energized by building from 0 to 1. All hiring decisions are made by our hiring team.\n\n\n\n\nABOUT THE ROLE\n\nFloat is hiring a Founding Lead to own and accelerate Float Intelligence end to end, across the technical foundations, the data, and the product experiences, all under a single mandate. Float Intelligence is how we bring agentic AI finance to every business in Canada: a product that does the finance work our customers do by hand today, coding transactions, chasing receipts, checking spend against policy, and gathering invoices out of inboxes and vendor portals. We shipped the first version this year and it worked. Now we are building the rest of it, and we are building it fast.\n\n\n\nYou would lead a small, fast-moving team of product engineers and data/ML engineers, reporting directly to the Head of Product. This is intentionally a hybrid seat across Engineering and Product leadership. You own the roadmap for what gets built, and you make the technical calls: model choice, evaluation, what has to be deterministic, and what a launch is gated on. The team ships into other product teams' surfaces and builds net-new surfaces that put AI directly in front of customers.\n\n\n\nThis is a true end-to-end owner role. The people who do best here are ex-founders and highly capable technical leaders with strong commercial product taste, opinionated about both what to build and how to build it, and drawn to the highest-leverage, most cutting-edge AI work across Float's entire product surface.\n\n\n\n\nWHAT YOU'LL BE RESPONSIBLE FOR\n\n - Leading, growing, and developing a small team of product engineers and data/ML engineers.\n\n - Owning the roadmap for Float's AI experiences alongside the Head of Product, including proposing new bets.\n\n - Taking AI products from zero to one, from exploratory proofs of concept through to the experiences that reach customers at scale.\n\n - Making the technical calls: model and LLM approach, evaluation design, and the infrastructure for scale, latency, and inference cost.\n\n - Building the shared platform layer, where required for: extraction, evaluation, observability, agent and prompt frameworks, and data pipelines, that other product teams build on rather than rebuild.\n\n - Equipping internal product teams with the AI models and engines they need to ship the experiences they want, and building new customer-facing surfaces that expose those experiences directly.\n\n - Partnering with the product managers whose areas these experiences ship into, so each one lands well and ownership is clear afterward.\n\n - Deciding what to stop, since exploratory work only pays off when the things that are not working get killed quickly.\n\n\n\n\nABOUT YOU\n\n\nHERE'S WHAT SETS YOU UP FOR SUCCESS AT FLOAT:\n\n - You Put Customers First, Always. You're energized by building from 0 to 1. You're not afraid to challenge the status quo, experiment quickly, and learn as you go.\n\n - You Constantly Learn and Grow. You're hungry to improve your craft and open to feedback. You bring a growth mindset to everything you do.\n\n - You Raise the Bar. You care about doing things well and efficiently. You balance speed with rigor and always look for ways to improve how we work.\n\n - You Win as a Team. You're a generous collaborator who values communication, context, and shared wins. You lift others up and help make the team stronger.\n\n\n\n\nIN ADDITION TO LIVING OUR VALUES, YOU BRING: \n\n - 7+ years in software engineering, including time at a company with a strong engineering culture where you reached a senior or staff level.\n\n - 2+ years managing engineers, ideally including people whose specialty is not your own.\n\n - Hands-on experience building and shipping AI or LLM-backed products to real users — not prototypes or internal experiments.\n\n - Past experience building 0→1 products or founding a software business.\n\n - Real depth in the parts that make AI products work in production: evaluation design, infrastructure at scale, latency, and managing inference cost with vendors.\n\n - A track record of building something 0→1, whether as a founder, an early engineer, or the person who started a product line inside a larger company.\n\n - Product instincts strong enough to own a roadmap: choosing what to build, sequencing it, and defending what you left out.\n\n - Comfort working across other teams' surfaces and getting alignment without formal authority.\n\n - Nice to have: experience fine-tuning models, or a data science or ML engineering background.\n\n\n\n\nTHIS MAY NOT BE THE ROLE FOR YOU IF: \n\n - You want a defined roadmap handed to you. And we’re looking for bold innovators to help shape the future of business finance in Canada.\n\n\n\n\nAI USE IN OUR HIRING PROCESS\n\nWe use technology, including artificial intelligence (AI), to support parts of our hiring process. This may include AI-assisted scheduling and candidate communications, and AI-generated interview notes, guides or summaries to help our team focus on the conversation. All hiring decisions are made by our hiring team.\n\n\n\n\nABOUT THE ROLE\n\nAs a Customer Success Manager, you’ll play a critical role in ensuring our customers successfully adopt and maximize the value of Float from the moment they onboard and throughout their journey. You’ll be a trusted partner, working closely with customers to drive strong adoption, mitigate risks, and unlock long-term growth opportunities.\n\n\n\nAt Float, we believe great customer success is about building meaningful partnerships and unlocking long-term value for our customers. If you’re passionate about driving adoption, mitigating risks, and helping businesses scale their financial operations, we’d love to hear from you!\n\n\n\nThis is a remote role based in Quebec. You'll work primarily from home, with occasional travel to our Toronto office for team gatherings, key meetings, and moments of in-person connection and collaboration.\n\n\n\n\nWHAT YOU'LL BE RESPONSIBLE FOR\n\n\nBUILDING AN EARLY FOUNDATION FOR LONG-TERM SUCCESS\n\n - Build deep relationships with customers as they begin their Float journey, ensuring a smooth and successful onboarding experience.\n\n - Partner with key stakeholders to define success criteria and measurable outcomes for their initial adoption of Float.\n\n - Identify long-term expansion opportunities by deeply understanding each customer’s broader financial operations and future needs.\n\n - Ensure customers stay on track with their year-one objectives, including spend targets and product adoption milestones.\n\n - Serve as a strategic partner post-onboarding to drive continued engagement, training, and advocacy within customer organizations.\n\n - Proactively monitor customer health signals and usage patterns, ensuring any barriers to adoption are addressed early.\n\n\nPROACTIVELY MANAGING RISK AND RETENTION\n\n - Identify risks across your book of business and develop proactive mitigation plans in partnership with cross-functional teams.\n\n - Ensure customers remain engaged and see ongoing value from Float by addressing potential churn indicators before they escalate.\n\n - Support customers through any transitions, ensuring they continue to leverage Float’s full capabilities.\n\n\nCHAMPIONING PRODUCT ADOPTION & DRIVING INNOVATION\n\n - Drive customer adoption of Float’s full suite of features, ensuring teams maximize the value of corporate and employee spend management.\n\n - Advocate for customer participation in Float’s Early Adopter Programs, gathering insights to shape future product iterations.\n\n - Educate and inspire customers to explore new ways to optimize their workflows with Float’s evolving capabilities.\n\n - Identify opportunities for growth across your aligned Book of Business. \n\n\nBEING THE VOICE OF THE CUSTOMER AT FLOAT\n\n - Provide insight and strategic recommendations on how Float can best serve our customers, from social proof to feature enhancements.\n\n - Partner with internal teams to leverage customer feedback for product development and operational improvements.\n\n - Help accelerate learning cycles by engaging customers who share our passion for simplifying corporate spending.\n\n - Collaborate on initiatives that impact Float’s customers, from onboarding programs to strategic campaigns that drive engagement and growth.\n\n - Support the development and execution of scalable processes that enhance the customer experience at every stage of their journey.\n\n\n\nAbout You\n\n\nHERE’S WHAT SETS YOU UP FOR SUCCESS AT FLOAT:\n\n - You Put Customers First, Always. You care deeply about delivering meaningful value. Whether you're building internal systems or customer-facing features, you're always thinking about how to make life better for our users.\n\n - You Act Like an Owner. You take responsibility for outcomes, step up to challenges, and seek solutions proactively—doing what’s best for the business, not just your role.\n\n - You Think Big and Move Fast. You’re energized by building from 0 to 1. You’re not afraid to challenge the status quo, experiment quickly, and learn as you go.\n\n - You Constantly Learn and Grow. You’re hungry to improve your craft and open to feedback. You bring a growth mindset to everything you do.\n\n - You Raise the Bar. You care about doing things well and efficiently. You balance speed with rigor and always look for ways to improve how we work.\n\n - You Win as a Team. You’re a generous collaborator who values communication, context, and shared wins. You lift others up and help make the team stronger.\n\n\n\n\nIN ADDITION TO LIVING OUR VALUES...\n\n - You're bilingual. You're fluent in both French and English — written and spoken — and can move effortlessly between the two with customers and colleagues across Canada.\n\n - You’ve got the experience. To be successful in this role, we’re looking for a Customer Success Manager with 3+ years of experience managing a book of 50+ customers simultaneously. You have a proven track record of driving product adoption, retention, and expansion within a B2B customer-base. \n   \n   - Nice to have: CPA, CA, CFA designation\n\n - You know how to leverage data. You prioritize your efforts based on insights—analyzing customer usage, engagement trends, and success metrics to focus on the highest-impact activities. You’re comfortable with using technology to forecast risk, drive adoption, and measure success.\n\n - You’re eager to continue learning. You take a curious and problem-solving approach to customer challenges, always seeking to understand the ‘why’ behind every issue. You’re resourceful, adaptable, and energized by finding creative solutions that drive customer success.\n\n - You believe the customer comes first. You’re a strong advocate for your customers and bring their voice into internal conversations to enhance their experience. You actively contribute to internal initiatives, such as playbook development, process improvements, or customer advocacy programs, to scale impact beyond your own book of business.\n\n - You understand the market. Experience working with finance, accounting, or payments-related products is a plus. You understand the commercial side of customer success, aligning customer needs with business goals and identifying win-win opportunities for expansion.\n\n\n\n\nTHIS MAY NOT BE THE ROLE FOR YOU IF: \n\n - You need close day-to-day direction rather than working independently\n\n - You’re not energized by feedback or fast-paced change\n\n - You’re seeking predictability over adaptability\n\n - You’re not comfortable making decisions in ambiguous situations\n\n - You prefer to stay in your lane rather than collaborate cross-functionally\n\n - You don’t feel a strong connection to Float’s mission or the product we’re building\n\n\n\n\nWHY YOU SHOULD JOIN\n\n - Work at one of Canada's fastest-growing fintech companies\n\n - Make a real impact in a high-autonomy, high-growth role\n\n - Collaborate with an ambitious and supportive team\n\n - Competitive compensation, equity options, and benefits\n\n - Hybrid work model – we are based in Toronto with in-office days for connection and collaboration\n\n - Enjoy catered team lunches every Tuesday, Wednesday and Thursday\n\n - Bring your pup to our dog-friendly office\n\n - Thrive in a high-trust, high-performance culture where your work truly matters\n\n \n\n\nIN SHORT\n\nAt Float, you’ll thrive if you’re bold, curious, and eager to make a real impact.
